date_note: Registered and scored between 8 and 10 October 2026; the exact day is not recorded in the report.
title: Model 2 on raw GPS trackers inside Sargassum mats (Barbados and Jamaica)
scope: Pre-registered test on open-data hourly GPS fixes from trackers inside Sargassum mats (Fidai et al. 2023), never used before and with nothing fitted: 5 trackers off Barbados (152 cases at 48 h) and 1 tracker off Jamaica (113 cases at 48 h).
summary: The recipe beat the old baseline on real mats. Barbados untracked: 21% lower miss at 48 h (-6.50 km, interval -9.78 to -3.43; medians 26.3 vs 29.7 km). Barbados tracked: 17% lower at 24 h and 19% lower at 48 h (-7.87 to -1.13 km interval; median 24.8 to 16.8 km), on raw fixes with no interpolation leak. Jamaica, a separate single-tracker registration, confirmed all three tests: untracked -21% at 48 h, tracked -26% at 24 h and -18% at 48 h. The 6 h tracked setting on Barbados did not confirm (-10%, interval -0.87 to +0.06 km).

limitations: The source report is an untracked working-tree file; it is identified by SHA-256 only and has no source commit.
Five trackers in one season and one area, plus one tracker off Jamaica; intervals resample tracker-days and are optimistic.
Forcing is reanalysis currents; no forecast fields.
It disagrees with the 2018 Puerto Rico mats, where a related blend family was worse than the cached baseline.
On Jamaica the extra 1% wind mattered (-21% for the wind-added recipe against -12% for the current-only one).
